fact_text: EPS equals net profit divided by total shares outstanding, and P/E equals share price divided by EPS; net profit is taken from the profit and loss statement.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: A snapshot's latest EPS shows only the most recent quarter, while annual EPS covers the full fiscal year, so the two figures should not be mixed up.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: Investors should decide on expected earnings rather than historical ones; analysts build expected EPS with different assumptions on inflation, taxation and the economy, so the forecast varies.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: PEG equals expected P/E divided by expected EPS growth in percent; below 1 the analyst reads a stock as undervalued, around 1 as fair and above 1 as overvalued, and warns not to rely on PEG alone.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: Expected EPS growth equals expected EPS minus current EPS, divided by current EPS, multiplied by 100 to express it as a percentage.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: Small changes in either share price or EPS move the P/E sharply, and a rising EPS lowers the P/E at any given share price.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: Stock splits, bonus shares and rights issues raise the share count and mechanically lower EPS, so an EPS drop should be checked against the share count before it is read as weaker business.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: When EPS falls sharply, the analyst says investors should find the cause: an economic shock such as the COVID period is different from a problem inside the company itself.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)

fact_text: A P/E should be read against the sector P/E and against growth, not on its own, because a low P/E alone can point towards a misleading conclusion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Analysis for Beginners (PSX) | Part 02 | How to Analyze EPS , P/E & PEG | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-01-24)
